analysis.title: Base Metals Comment: Blue Wave, Copper Ripples
key_insights: GS leaves its copper forecast unchanged at $15,400/t in 2027 (13% upside vs. spot) following the midterms, and flags two downside risks: AI-related positioning and US tariffs.

The forecast rests on two tightening forces expected to persist into 2027, continued US stockbuilding ahead of potential tariffs and China's scrap shortage, plus elevated investor positioning. The midterms put the first and last of these at risk.

LME copper has fallen about 7% over the past month to $13,588/t, driven largely by volatility in AI-related equities that sold off after the Democratic sweep. GS reads the correction as positioning-driven, not as looser fundamentals.

Physical fundamentals remain tight, especially in China. The Yangshan import premium is at a record high above $200/t, reflecting limited metal availability in China and outside the US, and ex-US inventories are at seasonal lows.

Combined COMEX and LME net length fell to about 9% of open interest last week from about 21% at end-September, well below the 16% GS assumes from 2027. If positioning stays at current levels, the GS model implies 2027 copper averaging about $14,600/t versus the $15,400/t forecast.

Copper has tracked the GS AI Data Center basket (mostly AI infrastructure suppliers such as semiconductors and electrical equipment makers) since late 2025. Copper positioning may stay subdued if equities price an earlier turn in the AI capex cycle, even while data center construction continues.

Data center moratoria are a delay risk with limited copper demand impact over the next two years. GS economists expect Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan to impose short-lived, conditional moratoria, which GS equity analysts expect to mainly affect new projects rather than those under construction.

Capacity already under construction is sufficient to meet GS's US data center additions forecast through 2028. A six-month delay of all under-construction Texas capacity would shift about 50kt of copper demand out of 2027 and cut the 2027 price forecast by at most about $100/t, to $15,300/t.
Data center risks are greater from 2029, when the forecast relies more on projects not yet under construction. Announced high-likelihood projects point to a pipeline well above what GS assumes.

The COMEX-LME spread implies a tariff duty of just 1% for January 2027 and about 6-7% for January 2028, which points to limited near-term tariff expectations. The GS forecast assumes about 400kt of US inventory overbuild in 2027.
If US stockbuilding stopped altogether, GS estimates copper would average about $14,500/t in 2027, with more downside if most of this year's US inventory build flowed back to the rest of the world.

The Democratic sweep does not eliminate tariff risk. The copper tariff decision is a presidential one under Section 232, rolling it back by legislation would need bipartisan support, and Democrats may not prioritize opposing refined copper tariffs in upcoming negotiations.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical fundamentals are tight: the Yangshan import premium is at a record above $200/t, ex-US inventories are at seasonal lows, and US stockbuilding and China's scrap shortage persist into 2027, supporting $15,400/t.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning has fallen to about 9% of open interest versus the 16% assumed, which implies about $14,600/t, and a stop in US stockbuilding implies about $14,500/t. The AI equity sell-off and low tariff expectations add pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Positioning staying at the current ~9% of open interest rather than recovering to the assumed 16% from 2027, or US stockbuilding stopping altogether.

theme_stances.key_argument: Physical fundamentals remain tight and the recent price correction is positioning-driven, so the 2027 forecast is unchanged with downside risks from AI positioning and US tariffs.
theme_stances.evidence: We see the recent correction as positioning-driven rather than reflecting loosening fundamentals.
